newsitem.title: USA: NFL-COWBOYS' SWITZER CHARGED IN AIRPORT GUN INCIDENT.
newsitem.headline: NFL-COWBOYS' SWITZER CHARGED IN AIRPORT GUN INCIDENT.

text.p: Dallas Cowboys head coach Barry Switzer faces up to a year in jail if convicted on a misdemeanor charge filed on Thursday for carrying a loaded gun through Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport.

Prosecutors for the Tarrant County District Attorney's office said Switzer would be tried at a still undetermined date on the charge of unlawfully carrying a weapon, which carries a maximum punishment of a year in jail and a fine up to $4,000.
The misdemeanor was a break for Switzer, who could have faced the felony charge of carrying a weapon into an airport, which carries a maximum punishment of 10 years behind bars.
Assistant district attorney Robert Mayfield said the lesser charge was chosen because Switzer had no previous criminal record and appeared to have no "ulterior motive" in carrying the gun.

Switzer, in his fourth year as the Cowboys coach, was arrested on Monday at the airport when a .38 calibre handgun was found in his carry-on luggage as he walked through a security checkpoint before boarding a plane for Austin, Texas.

He apologised for the incident and said he had no idea the gun was in the bag. He said he hid it there last Saturday because there were three children visiting his house, and that he forgot to take it out later.

On Wednesday, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones fined Switzer $75,000 for the incident, which ran contrary to Jones' recent attempts to clean up the Cowboys' less than wholesome image following several unsavory off-the-field incidents in the last few years.
